---
applyTo: "packages/genui/ui-judge/**/*"
---

Keep UI Judge a Rust-only crate. Its public API, model integration, tests, and user examples belong under `packages/genui/ui-judge`; do not add an npm package manifest, TypeScript facade, or JavaScript test suite back to this directory. The default feature set remains library-only. The `server` feature owns the `ui-judge-server` binary and HTTP process adapter. The existing ReactLynx fixture source is a runtime asset consumed by the repository's headless runner, not a JavaScript UI Judge API or test harness. Keep the fallback model at `gpt-4o-mini` unless its ownership contract is deliberately changed; an explicit `UI_JUDGE_MODEL` must continue to override that default. UI Judge owns its model and the corresponding `UI_JUDGE_API_KEY`, `UI_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, and `UI_JUDGE_API_STYLE` connection tuple. GenUI Server Bench must know only its sidecar URL and must neither mirror, configure, nor validate those model settings.

Keep the default crate-root API restricted to `judge_page`, `JudgePageRequest`, `UiJudgeResult`, and `UiJudgeError`; the `server` feature may additionally expose its server module. The request uses only standard-library field types and always performs visual-correctness scoring internally. `JudgePageRequest::include_geqi` may additionally run the four weighted GEQI dimensions against the same final screenshot; keep their identifiers, labels, criteria, order, and weights internal rather than exporting dimension-selection or prompt APIs. Do not export model clients, model options, runner types, screenshot helpers, prompts, parsers, GEQI dimension types, fixture helpers, or screenshot-comparison APIs.

Keep the feature-gated server protocol at `GET /health`, `POST /judge`, `POST /screenshot/lynxml`, `POST /screenshot/template/url`, `POST /screenshot/zip/upload`, `POST /screenshot/zip/url`, and `POST /compare`; do not restore the generic `POST /screenshot` route. Reject direct `file://`, `http://`, and `https://` page URLs on the JSON judge route with `403` before model initialization or headless capture. Trusted callers may continue to use the default library API for direct URL judging. Give every source-specific screenshot route the same required `entry` query, accepting a safe relative staged path or equivalent `zip://` URL while never accepting a caller-supplied base directory, model option, or interaction step. The LynXML screenshot route accepts a raw UTF-8 body with an XML or plain-text media type and stages it at the requested `.lynxml` entry. The ZIP upload route accepts a raw `application/zip` body; the ZIP URL and template URL routes accept an HTTP(S) URL in a raw `text/plain` body, fetch it through the shared SSRF-safe downloader, and apply the same 10 MiB source limit. The shared downloader must reject credentials and non-HTTP(S) schemes, disable redirects and ambient proxies, validate every resolved address as public, and pin those validated addresses for the connection to prevent DNS rebinding. Resolve staged inputs through the headless resource fetcher against the internally injected canonical directory; do not duplicate its path policy in the HTTP adapter. Buffer at most 10 MiB with a ten-second total body-read deadline even when `Content-Length` is absent or false, then wait asynchronously for one of the four isolated-render slots before staging or extraction. Transfer the staging guard, requested internal URL, and render slot to a supervisor that starts one fresh `ui-judge-server` capture child for that source; on request cancellation or timeout, kill and reap the child before dropping the guard, and drain all supervisors during server shutdown. The comparison route accepts exactly one `referenceImage` and one `renderedImage` multipart upload, applies the existing image limits, and runs only deterministic normalization, alignment, and pixel comparison; it must not initialize a model client or enqueue headless rendering. Read `LYNX_USE_PORT` with a default of `8080`, reject zero, and bind separate IPv4 and IPv6 unspecified listeners. Have `build.rs` generate an executable `start.sh` in the Cargo profile output directory that starts the colocated `ui-judge-server` binary, copy the target Lynx runtime and `lynx_core.js` into the same runnable output layout, and package those generated assets rather than recovering them independently in `build.sh`. Obtain the default core script through the shared, SHA-256-verified artifact downloader rather than a checked-in fixture; honor `LYNX_CORE_JS_PATH` as a local build-time source while retaining the platform-standard packaged destination name. The server binary should select the packaged runtime when the caller has not set `LYNX_LIB_PATH` or `LYNX_SDK_DIR`, so the launcher stays a simple colocated executable wrapper. Accept HTTP connections concurrently, but run any trusted non-upload library page lifecycle sequentially through one process-wide capture broker whose dedicated owner thread reuses one `LynxContainer`. Untrusted staged-source capture is the deliberate exception: every request owns one short-lived child process and one container so Clay's process-global resource caches cannot cross tenants. Do not reintroduce a `LocalSet`, a `JoinSet` of ordinary capture futures, multiple long-lived production capture brokers, or multiple native container owners in one process. Use a bounded capture queue whose callers wait asynchronously for capacity within their request timeout, without blocking a Tokio worker. Do not reject requests merely because a capture or isolated-render queue is currently full; eager admission control and load shedding belong in outer middleware. Return `503` only when no live slot can become available because the worker is unavailable or shutting down. The owner worker may bridge to the async model client with one current-thread runtime; that is the only async allowed on the ordinary native side. After capture returns an owned BMP, run VLM scoring and reference comparison concurrently across judge requests. Limit request bodies and gracefully drain the HTTP server, all child supervisors, and the headless worker on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Treat a headless-worker panic as fatal: atomically stop admission, drop queued jobs so their handlers can drain, mark readiness unhealthy, initiate shutdown, and propagate the join failure from the server task.

Build the UI Judge container for `linux/amd64`, matching the downloaded Lynx runtime ABI. Keep `packages/genui/ui-judge/Dockerfile` runtime-only: give it the bundle produced by `build.sh` as its build context, copy only the generated server, launcher, core script, and runtime library, install `libepoxy0` and `libexpat1`, and run the image as a non-root user. Pin the Ubuntu tag to a reviewed OCI index digest that contains a `linux/amd64` manifest. Keep model credentials outside image layers. Production deployments must combine the image with the read-only-root and dedicated temporary-volume containment described below.

Keep untrusted ZIP staging in the server-feature `src/zip/` module and never accept a client-supplied extraction directory. Reject uploads above 10 MiB before parsing, archives with more than 100 entries, overlapping entries, encryption, unsafe or duplicate paths, path/file collisions, symlinks and non-file/non-directory Unix types. Do not rely only on `ZipArchive::len()` for the count or duplicate checks: `zip` 8.6 stores entries by raw name and silently replaces exact duplicates, so also validate the structural central-directory entry count. Before constructing `ZipArchive`, accept only the rightmost classic EOCD whose comment ends exactly at EOF, reject ZIP64 sentinels and ZIP64 local or central extra fields, and structurally prove that the central directory ends at that EOCD with no more than 100 entries. Hide local headers and file data from the library's metadata fallback scan and reject extra EOCD signatures in the visible central-directory and comment region, so a malformed outer record cannot fall back to metadata embedded in an ordinary nested ZIP. Limit each file to 50 MiB, the archive output to 100 MiB, path depth to 20, components to 255 bytes, relative paths to 4096 bytes, and both declared and actually written compression ratios to 100:1. Extract through a fixed 64 KiB buffer into a fresh private `TempDir`, create files exclusively, count actual writes, propagate CRC/read failures, and remove the complete staging directory on every failure. Nested ZIP files remain ordinary files.

Run synchronous ZIP work through `spawn_blocking` with a separate four-permit semaphore and a ten-second absolute deadline. Wait asynchronously for an extraction permit within that same deadline; do not reserve extraction capacity in the HTTP adapter before buffering an upload. A timed-out blocking task cannot be forcibly stopped, so move its permit and temporary-directory guard into the blocking closure and check the same deadline between entries, reads, and writes; do not release capacity when only the async join wait times out. A successful `ExtractedZip` owns its staged-tree guard but not the shorter-lived extraction permit. ZIP-backed capture must inject the canonical base directory internally, acquire an isolated-render slot before extraction, and move the extraction guard and render slot into its one-shot child supervisor, which bounds staged trees and active renders to four. A full renderer or ordinary capture queue must leave the HTTP request future waiting until capacity or its deadline; rely on outer middleware for eager load shedding. Use a minimal child environment, null stdout and stderr, a private parent-liveness pipe on stdin, a private exclusive output file, and one absolute render deadline that also covers queue waiting, extraction, output reading, and JPEG transcoding. Preserve the trusted temporary-volume variables and coverage profile variable without forwarding model credentials. Cancellation and timeout must kill and positively reap the child before releasing staging capacity, while parent death must close the lifeline and terminate the child. Bound reaping by a short fixed grace; if process control still cannot confirm it, terminate the service without unwinding the staging guard or requesting a core dump, and rely on the service supervisor to restart it. Deployment must add the hard containment process isolation cannot provide: a non-root account, read-only root filesystem, disabled core dumps, cgroup/container CPU, memory, and process limits, and a dedicated `noexec,nosuid,nodev` temporary volume with an ephemeral-storage quota sized for four bounded extractions. Record only sanitized archive byte/entry/declared-size/actual-size/duration/outcome metrics plus a trusted job identity, never raw entry names or free-form tasks.

The runner captures frames as uncompressed BMP. Keep that lossless copy for the deterministic reference comparison and transcode to JPEG only for bytes that leave the process — the VLM data URL and source-specific screenshot responses — because vision models do not accept `image/bmp`. Composite transparent pixels over white when transcoding.

Keep reference-image comparison inside the Rust crate and reachable through `JudgePageRequest::reference_image`. Preserve `reference` as textual model context; accept reference images as plain base64, base64 data URLs, or HTTP(S) URLs, with explicit compressed-byte, decoded-dimension, pixel-count, and allocation limits. After the final screenshot is captured, run the VLM evaluations and reference-image comparison as independent chains that share only the captured frame. Every VLM evaluation always scores that single screenshot from `task` and textual `reference`; never send the reference image, alignment result, pixel diff, or deterministic similarity to a VLM. The reference-image chain must only load and normalize the baseline, align it with normalized cross-correlation, and compute block-based pixel differences and a diff image. Run bounded alignment and pixel-diff work off the async runtime. Keep top-level `score`, `reason`, and `summary` owned by the visual-correctness VLM; keep each GEQI dimension's score, reason, summary, and error independent, preserve the 30/25/15/15 relative weighting normalized to a 0-100 result, and do not let a dimension failure overwrite the visual-correctness result. Report reference-image failures separately without overwriting VLM output, and preserve successful comparison diagnostics when VLM scoring fails. Expose only standard-type diagnostics on `UiJudgeResult`; keep alignment, comparison, artifact, prompt, and algorithm types private to the crate.

Preserve the former TypeScript reference-comparison semantics during migration work: successful alignment compares the overlap crop, fallback comparison normalizes both images to their minimum dimensions with fill-style resizing, and pixel distance compares all four raw RGBA channels. Penalizing non-overlap or premultiplying alpha is a separate metric change, not a migration cleanup. Run CPU-heavy post-capture image work, including BMP-to-JPEG transcoding, on a bounded Rayon pool off the async runtime. Keep a permit with each Rayon job until the CPU work actually ends, even if its async waiter is dropped, so cancelled requests cannot overbook the pool.

Do not modify or duplicate `lynx-headless-rust-test-runner` as part of UI Judge work. `judge_page` must accept only `file://`, `http://`, and `https://` URLs; reject bare paths and other schemes before initializing the model or headless runtime. Internally use the runner's existing navigation, DOM, selector tap, wait, and software screenshot APIs. Keep model creation inside `judge_page` and the container and page lifecycle inside the single-owner capture worker. Do not re-export `LynxContainer`, `LynxPage`, or other runner implementation types or require callers to construct them. `judge_page` must stay callable from any runtime, including a current-thread one, because native work never runs on the caller's thread. Preserve natural-language `steps` by using Agent SDK to choose selector taps and waits from the current DOM and screenshot; report swipe, scrolling, typing, and coordinate touch as unsupported because the existing runner does not expose them. Do not add Kitten-Lynx, Android, ADB, an emulator, Playwright, or a browser as a UI Judge runtime dependency.

Keep `JudgePageRequest::timeout` compatible with the former TypeScript API: it is a per-operation and per-step limit, not an overall request deadline. Connection, navigation, each natural-language step, final screenshot capture, visual-correctness scoring, each enabled GEQI dimension, and optional reference-image comparison each receive the full duration; document that distinction wherever the request API is shown.

Use Agent SDK for structured VLM evaluation. Keep any OpenAI-compatible transport adapter in Rust and use only the documented `UI_JUDGE_API_KEY`, `UI_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `UI_JUDGE_MODEL`, `UI_JUDGE_API_STYLE`, and `UI_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS` model environment-variable inputs. Do not accept legacy Midscene- or OpenAI-prefixed variables, JSON init config, or model-family configuration, and do not add a Midscene runtime dependency. Keep unit tests deterministic with `UI_JUDGE_MODEL_RESPONSE_JSON`. The runtime-backed `headless_e2e` integration test is intentionally different: it must reject mock-response variables unconditionally. It must skip inside the test when `UI_JUDGE_API_KEY` is absent or empty; otherwise it must call the real model supplied through the injected model environment.

Keep 0-5 score normalization and typed page result structures in the Rust library. Keep top-level `score` as the backward-compatible visual-correctness result; expose the optional weighted aggregate separately as `geqi_score` from 0 through 100. Do not add result-file generation, a UI Judge PR-comment action, or a GitHub comment publishing workflow.

Keep concurrent-request coverage fixed-size and behavioral: submit four distinct fixture bundles concurrently through the production single-owner worker, validate each screenshot, and do not add duration, QPS, latency, or throughput assertions.

Keep the existing React Lynx fixture at `packages/genui/ui-judge/tests/fixtures/react`, because the unchanged headless runner reads that path. Build its `.lynx.bundle` into the ignored `.generated/` directory and never commit generated bundle binaries.
